title: Two vendor names that differ only in capitals keep one order everywhere
custom_preconds:
Setup file (for Claude sessions; a tester does not need it)

Preconditions

  • You are signed in as a user with the "Admin" role, with {Location-A} as your current location.
    For example: {Location-A} is Staging Heavy Duty - 9919.
  • Two vendors have open bills on today's date and their names differ only in capitals: {Vendor-A} and {Vendor-B}.
    For example: {Vendor-A} is ZZAUTOTEST S1-06 Ace Towing and {Vendor-B} is ZZAUTOTEST S1-06 ACE TOWING.
  • Starting screen: Reports > Finance > A/P Summary is open in a desktop browser window 1440 px wide, as opened from the Reports menu.
  • If any record above is missing, mark this test Blocked: "setup not done".
custom_steps:
1. Find {Vendor-A} and {Vendor-B} in the list and note which one is higher.
  2. Choose "Download (PDF)" from the ⋯ menu at the right of the title.
  3. Open the PDF and find the two names.
  4. Choose "Download (CSV)" from the ⋯ menu.
  5. Open the CSV in a spreadsheet program and find the two names.
  6. Reload the page and find the two names again.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Step 1: the two vendors sit next to each other (no other vendor between them) in one order.
  • Step 2: the PDF downloads.
  • Step 3: the two names are in the same order as on screen.
  • Step 4: the CSV downloads.
  • Step 5: the two rows are in the same order as on screen.
  • Step 6: after the reload they are still in the same order.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "A/R and A/P Report Sorting, Export and Location Filter", Confluence 947650561, version 5 (21 Oct 2026, Chris Ward), read 22 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-11315, story SV-11531 (Story 1, Reports open in QuickBooks name order), story SV-11533 (Story 3, Export to PDF and CSV)

  • S1-R4: “Two names that compare equal are ordered by the plain lower-cased name, then by the customer or vendor itself, so the same two customers always come out in the same order on screen, in the PDF and in the CSV.”
  • S1-R2: “Name order compares names ignoring capitals, in plain character order: digits and punctuation compare as characters, so "10 Trucking" comes before "2 Trucking" and "A-1 Towing" before "a1 towing".”
  • S3-R2: “The PDF downloads as a file.”
